title: Quasi-inverse with prescribed object representatives and comparisons
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be categories [def-nagata-category] small in a common sufficiently large universe and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be fully faithful: its maps on all morphism sets are bijections. Suppose that for every object $X$ of $\mathcal B$ an object $j(X)$ of $\mathcal A$ and an isomorphism $i_X:X\xrightarrow{\sim}F(j(X))$ are specified. There is a unique functor $J:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ with $J(X)=j(X)$ such that the specified $i_X$ are the components of a natural isomorphism $i:1_{\mathcal B}\xrightarrow{\sim}FJ$. Its arrow map is characterized by $F(J(f))=i_Y\circ f\circ i_X^{-1}$ for $f:X\to Y$. Moreover there is a natural isomorphism $e:JF\xrightarrow{\sim}1_{\mathcal A}$ characterized by $F(e_A)=i_{F(A)}^{-1}$ for every $A$. In particular $F$ and $J$ are quasi-inverse equivalences.

source.place: Tag 05SG, lemma-construct-quasi-inverse; the final comparison e is the isomorphism constructed in its proof.

proof.text: For each pair $A,A'$ write $p_{A,A'}$ for the inverse of the stipulated bijection $F:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(A,A')\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(FA,FA')$. Set $J(X)=j(X)$ and, for $f:X\to Y$, set $J(f)=p_{j(X),j(Y)}(i_Y\circ f\circ i_X^{-1})$. Thus $F(J(f))=i_Y\circ f\circ i_X^{-1}$, with the required source and target. These are inverse functions of specified bijections of sets, in the fixed universe; no new object representatives are chosen.

The category laws [def-nagata-category] give $F(J(1_X))=i_X\circ1_X\circ i_X^{-1}=1_{Fj(X)}=F(1_{j(X)})$. For $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$, functoriality of $F$ gives
$$F(J(g)\circ J(f))=(i_Z\circ g\circ i_Y^{-1})\circ(i_Y\circ f\circ i_X^{-1})=i_Z\circ(g\circ f)\circ i_X^{-1}=F(J(g\circ f)).$$
Injectivity of the relevant Hom maps proves both functor laws, so the data define $J$.

source.place: Tag 05SG, lemma-construct-quasi-inverse, proof; omitted functor-law verification expanded

proof.text: The arrow formula gives $F(J(f))\circ i_X=i_Y\circ f$, so the prescribed components define a natural transformation $i:1_{\mathcal B}\to FJ$. Multiplying this equality by the inverse components gives $f\circ i_X^{-1}=i_Y^{-1}\circ F(J(f))$; hence those inverses are natural as well and $i$ is a natural isomorphism. If $J'$ has the prescribed object map and makes these same components natural, its naturality forces $F(J'(f))=i_Y\circ f\circ i_X^{-1}=F(J(f))$. Faithfulness gives equality on arrows; the object maps already agree, proving uniqueness of the functor.

Take the natural isomorphism $\beta:FJF\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ obtained by evaluating $i^{-1}$ on $F(A)$; its component is $\beta_A=i_{F(A)}^{-1}$. Naturality is the inverse-naturality equality of the preceding step at the arrow $F(a)$ for $a:A\to A'$. Apply [lem-sfb-fully-faithful-cancel-iso-components] with source $\mathcal A$, the two functors $JF,1_{\mathcal A}$, and postcomposition functor $F$. It yields a natural isomorphism $e:JF\xrightarrow{\sim}1_{\mathcal A}$ satisfying $F(e_A)=\beta_A=i_{F(A)}^{-1}$. These equations determine each component uniquely by faithfulness. Together with $i^{-1}:FJ\xrightarrow{\sim}1_{\mathcal B}$, this is precisely the asserted pair of quasi-inverse equivalences.
